title: Tăng trưởng hay chất lượng sống · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering judging governments by wellbeing indicators rather than economic growth alone. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

vocabulary.example: Whether judging governments by wellbeing indicators rather than economic growth alone deserves priority depends on more than its intended benefit.
vocabulary.note: GDP đo sản lượng chứ không trừ tự động thời gian đi lại hoặc tổn thất không khí. Ví dụ tăng trưởng kèm đi làm xa chứng minh chỉ số kinh tế chưa đủ để suy ra đời sống tốt hơn. Cụm này gọi đúng cơ chế riêng của chính sách; cần giữ nghĩa trong ví dụ, không dùng thay cho việc giải thích quan hệ nhân quả.

paragraphs: National income records economic activity, but it cannot show by itself whether daily life is becoming healthier or less stressful. The main problem is that broad indicators may be difficult to compare and easy to select for political convenience; a transparent dashboard should supplement rather than erase conventional economic statistics.

Broad indicators may be difficult to compare and easy to select for political convenience. Wellbeing includes several dimensions that may move in opposite directions and are not easily reduced to one comparable number. A minister could highlight improving income while omitting deteriorating air quality, allowing the choice of indicators to conceal precisely the losses that a broader assessment was intended to reveal. A government able to change weights or publish only favourable measures can present a reassuring picture while avoiding scrutiny of worsening conditions.

A transparent dashboard should supplement rather than erase conventional economic statistics. An independent statistical body could publish fixed definitions and historical series for every indicator, requiring governments to explain deteriorating results instead of replacing inconvenient measures with more favourable ones. Presenting each dimension separately would let citizens see when an apparent overall improvement depends on offsetting deteriorating health with higher income, making the government's chosen trade-off available for public challenge. A stable and transparent set of measures reduces selective reporting, while retaining output data helps reveal whether proposed wellbeing gains rest on sustainable resources. A published dashboard should expose trade-offs between income, health and time while retaining economic statistics, rather than allow governments to select whichever indicator flatters their record.

A broader assessment is therefore preferable because growth can coexist with worsening lives; its credibility depends on publishing the same indicators consistently and showing the economic resources needed to sustain improvements in wellbeing.
